opening.text: Imagine a notebook with a page full of crossed-out lines and ink blots. You don't have to keep writing on that page. You can turn it. The next page is clean. The old page is still there, but it doesn't have to be where we write today. That's what a new beginning feels like.

mainMessage.text: Through Jesus Christ, we can turn the page and begin again.

blocks.text: **A clean page is offered** The Savior doesn't ask us to erase our past by ourselves. He offers the clean page.
Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
All of us can have a new beginning through, and because of, Jesus Christ.
The page is offered.
**More than one page** A notebook has many pages. God doesn't hand us just one.
Yea, and as often as my people repent will I forgive them their trespasses against me.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Jesus gives us as many new beginnings as we need.
There are many pages.
**The joy of a fresh start** Starting again isn't only a duty. It is a gift, and it brings joy.

And I also thank my God, yea, my great God, that he hath granted unto us that we might repent of these things, and also that he hath forgiven us of those our many sins and murders which we have committed, and taken away the guilt from our hearts, through the merits of his Son.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Repentance is not only possible but also joyful because of our Savior.
There is joy in it.
**Turning the page takes a hand** We turn the page by repenting. We name what was wrong and turn away from it.

Behold, he who has repented of his sins, the same is forgiven, and I, the Lord, remember them no more. By this ye may know if a man repenteth of his sins—behold, he will confess them and forsake them.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Repentance opens the door to our new beginnings, fresh starts, and second chances.
Repentance turns the page.
**Another chance, because of Him** We don't earn the clean page on our own. It comes because the Savior paid for our mistakes.

Now the Spirit knoweth all things; nevertheless the Son of God suffereth according to the flesh that he might take upon him the sins of his people, that he might blot out their transgressions according to the power of his deliverance; and now behold, this is the testimony which is in me.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we have another chance.
He made it possible.
**You are not the old page** The old blots don't define the person writing now.

And the Lord said unto me: Marvel not that all mankind, yea, men and women, all nations, kindreds, tongues and people, must be born again; yea, born of God, changed from their carnal and fallen state, to a state of righteousness, being redeemed of God, becoming his sons and daughters;
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
You don’t have to be who you’ve been before.
You can be new.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they started again after a mistake. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The son who came home

blocks.text: A son had wasted everything. He walked home, not knowing what his father would say.

And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
The father ran. He didn't wait for the speech to be finished. That is how God receives us.

application.text: First, think of one mistake that still weighs on you. Second, pray and tell Heavenly Father about it honestly. Third, take one step to make it right, and speak with your bishop or branch president if it is a serious matter.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ gives us a clean page. I know the Father runs to meet us. I know we can begin again. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: You take a wrong turn. The GPS says one thing: "Recalculating." It doesn't scold you. It doesn't tell you what a poor driver you are. It simply finds a new way from where you are now. That's how the Savior treats us after a mistake. Not a lecture. A new route.

mainMessage.text: The Savior recalculates from where we are. He doesn't scold. He gives a new route.

blocks.text: **The route is still open** A wrong turn doesn't end the trip. A new beginning is still possible.
Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
All of us can have a new beginning through, and because of, Jesus Christ.
The route is open.
**He recalculates as often as needed** The GPS doesn't run out of patience. Neither does the Lord.
Yea, and as often as my people repent will I forgive them their trespasses against me.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Jesus gives us as many new beginnings as we need.
He doesn't run out.
**Glad to be back on track** There's relief when the road makes sense again. Repentance brings that kind of joy.

And I also thank my God, yea, my great God, that he hath granted unto us that we might repent of these things, and also that he hath forgiven us of those our many sins and murders which we have committed, and taken away the guilt from our hearts, through the merits of his Son.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Repentance is not only possible but also joyful because of our Savior.
There is relief and joy.
**Make the turn** The GPS can only help if we turn. Repentance means we confess, we forsake, and we turn.

Behold, he who has repented of his sins, the same is forgiven, and I, the Lord, remember them no more. By this ye may know if a man repenteth of his sins—behold, he will confess them and forsake them.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Repentance opens the door to our new beginnings, fresh starts, and second chances.
Make the turn.
**The map was paid for** Someone paid for this route. Because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we have another chance.

Now the Spirit knoweth all things; nevertheless the Son of God suffereth according to the flesh that he might take upon him the sins of his people, that he might blot out their transgressions according to the power of his deliverance; and now behold, this is the testimony which is in me.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we have another chance.
He paid for it.
**Not the same driver** After a wrong turn, a good driver learns. We don't have to stay the person who made the mistake.

And the Lord said unto me: Marvel not that all mankind, yea, men and women, all nations, kindreds, tongues and people, must be born again; yea, born of God, changed from their carnal and fallen state, to a state of righteousness, being redeemed of God, becoming his sons and daughters;
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
You don’t have to be who you’ve been before.
You can change.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they got back on the right road. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Peter is restored

blocks.text: Peter had denied that he knew Jesus. Then the Savior found him by the sea.

Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew. So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
The Savior didn't dwell on the denial. He asked Peter about his love, and gave him work to do.

application.text: First, think about a past wrong turn you still carry. Second, ask Heavenly Father what the next right step is. Third, take it, and leave the rest to the Savior.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior doesn't scold us back onto the road. I know He gives us new routes. I know His love is patient. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A favorite bowl falls and cracks. Most people would throw it out. But in some places, craftsmen mend a broken bowl with gold. The cracks aren't hidden. They become part of the bowl. It may even be more valuable than before. The Savior mends us in a similar way. He doesn't throw us away.

mainMessage.text: The Savior mends what is broken. We are not thrown away.

blocks.text: **The Mender offers** The broken bowl doesn't mend itself. The Savior offers to do it.
Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
All of us can have a new beginning through, and because of, Jesus Christ.
He offers to mend us.
**Mended again and again** The Mender doesn't say, "Never again." He mends as often as we come.
Yea, and as often as my people repent will I forgive them their trespasses against me.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Jesus gives us as many new beginnings as we need.
He mends as often as needed.

Repentance is not only possible but also joyful because of our Savior.
Wholeness brings joy.
**We bring the pieces** We can't be mended if we hide the pieces. We bring them to Him. We confess and forsake.

Behold, he who has repented of his sins, the same is forgiven, and I, the Lord, remember them no more. By this ye may know if a man repenteth of his sins—behold, he will confess them and forsake them.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Repentance opens the door to our new beginnings, fresh starts, and second chances.
Bring the pieces.
**He paid for the gold** Mending cost Him. The Atonement of Jesus Christ is what pays for our second chance.

Now the Spirit knoweth all things; nevertheless the Son of God suffereth according to the flesh that he might take upon him the sins of his people, that he might blot out their transgressions according to the power of his deliverance; and now behold, this is the testimony which is in me.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we have another chance.
He paid for it.
**A new bowl, with a history** The mended bowl isn't what it was. It's stronger. We don't have to stay who we were.

And the Lord said unto me: Marvel not that all mankind, yea, men and women, all nations, kindreds, tongues and people, must be born again; yea, born of God, changed from their carnal and fallen state, to a state of righteousness, being redeemed of God, becoming his sons and daughters;
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).

You can be changed.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they were mended after a hard failure. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jonah gets a second call

blocks.text: Jonah had run from what God asked him to do. Then God spoke to him again.

And the word of the Lord came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee. So Jonah arose, and went unto Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an exceeding great city of three days’ journey.
The word came "the second time." God didn't give up on Jonah. Jonah arose and went.

application.text: First, think of a failure you'd rather hide. Second, bring it to Heavenly Father in prayer. Third, do the next right thing He puts in your heart.

But the whole yard looks different. That's what forgiveness feels like. The Lord said our sins can become white as snow.

Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

All of us can have a new beginning through, and because of, Jesus Christ.

Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).

Behold, he who has repented of his sins, the same is forgiven, and I, the Lord, remember them no more. By this ye may know if a man repenteth of his sins—behold, he will confess them and forsake them.

Now the Spirit knoweth all things; nevertheless the Son of God suffereth according to the flesh that he might take upon him the sins of his people, that he might blot out their transgressions according to the power of his deliverance; and now behold, this is the testimony which is in me.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt forgiven and clean. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma finds mercy

blocks.text: Alma had fought against the Church. In his deepest pain, he remembered the Savior.

Now, as my mind caught hold upon this thought, I cried within my heart: O Jesus, thou Son of God, have mercy on me, who am in the gall of bitterness, and am encircled about by the everlasting chains of death. And now, behold, when I thought this, I could remember my pains no more; yea, I was harrowed up by the memory of my sins no more. And oh, what joy, and what marvelous light I did behold; yea, my soul was filled with joy as exceeding as was my pain!
Alma cried out. The pain gave way to joy. The same mercy is open to us.

application.text: First, ask what is still "muddy" in your life that you could bring to the Lord. Second, pray for mercy, and for the strength to forsake it. Third, accept the forgiveness by living differently this week.

opening.text: Watch a toddler learn to walk. She stands. She wobbles. She falls. And what does she do? She doesn't say, "I'm no good at this." She gets up and tries again. Nobody thinks less of her. Everyone cheers. God watches us like that. When we fall, He doesn't turn away. He waits for us to stand again.

mainMessage.text: When we fall, God doesn't turn away. He cheers us on as we stand again.

blocks.text: **Every walker falls** No one learns to walk without falling. No one lives without mistakes. The Savior's offer is for all.
Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
All of us can have a new beginning through, and because of, Jesus Christ.
Everyone falls.
**More than one try** She doesn't get one try. She gets as many as she needs. So do we.
Yea, and as often as my people repent will I forgive them their trespasses against me.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Jesus gives us as many new beginnings as we need.
Many tries.
**The grin when she stands** A toddler beams when she gets up. Repentance can bring that kind of joy.

And I also thank my God, yea, my great God, that he hath granted unto us that we might repent of these things, and also that he hath forgiven us of those our many sins and murders which we have committed, and taken away the guilt from our hearts, through the merits of his Son.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Repentance is not only possible but also joyful because of our Savior.
Get up with joy.
**Get up, don't stay down** The toddler doesn't stay on the floor. Repenting means we get up: we confess and turn away from what was wrong.

Behold, he who has repented of his sins, the same is forgiven, and I, the Lord, remember them no more. By this ye may know if a man repenteth of his sins—behold, he will confess them and forsake them.
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
Repentance opens the door to our new beginnings, fresh starts, and second chances.
Get up.
**A hand to hold** A parent's hand is there. The Savior's hand is there, because He paid for our mistakes. Because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we have another chance.

Now the Spirit knoweth all things; nevertheless the Son of God suffereth according to the flesh that he might take upon him the sins of his people, that he might blot out their transgressions according to the power of his deliverance; and now behold, this is the testimony which is in me.
Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Repentance: A Joyful Choice” from the October 2016 general conference (Sunday Afternoon Session).
Because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, we have another chance.
Take His hand.
**Not a crawler forever** The toddler grows into a runner. We aren't stuck at the place of our worst day.

And the Lord said unto me: Marvel not that all mankind, yea, men and women, all nations, kindreds, tongues and people, must be born again; yea, born of God, changed from their carnal and fallen state, to a state of righteousness, being redeemed of God, becoming his sons and daughters;
Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Evening Session).
You don’t have to be who you’ve been before.
You will grow.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they fell and got up again. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Saul becomes Paul

blocks.text: Saul had fought against the Church. Then the Lord called him to a new work.

But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.
The Lord didn't see only Saul's past. He saw what Paul could become. He sees the same in us.

application.text: First, forgive yourself for one past mistake you've already repented of. Second, thank Heavenly Father for another chance. Third, do one good thing today that the old you wouldn't have done.
